report.summary: Twenty capture-compare-fix passes on the city, the map, the car HUD, water and atmosphere, judged against GTA V, Asphalt, Forza and Cyberpunk. The M map now beats GTA V's on features (aerial and atlas views, building layer, GPS that re-plans with turn-by-turn), the car shows nitro, brake and speed telemetry, and the late passes run at 115 FPS at 1440p with night reflections fixed.

map: Aerial view. The real city from above with building shadows, roads by class, district borders and decluttered icons.
GPS route. Right-click a waypoint: the route follows the road graph, with distance and ETA.
Atlas view (V). A clean road-map style with light building blocks.
Satnav panel. Next turn, distance and street over the minimap, with radar building blocks.
car: Pass 18 cluster. The dial sat too low and the nitro hint ran over the speed.
Nitro. Exhaust flames, light streaks, speed lines, boost-tinted cluster with cells, mode and gain pop-ups.
Brakes at dusk. Light trails, BRAKE/ABS lamps, pedal bars and per-wheel brake temperature.
Speed trap. Camera flash, measured speed, star rating and session best.
Rain night. Lens droplets; the wet street now stays dark with light reflections.
world_pairs: Pass 18. Windows noise, flat light at 18.3 h.
Pass 30. True golden hour, sun haze, roof finishes, parapets, solar rows.
Pass 18. An even wall of lit windows.
Pass 30. Occupancy per block, three light temperatures, lobbies.
Pass 30. Calm inland water, shallows and foam.
world: Night river. Dark water with warm city glints (it glowed blue before pass 33).
Road wear control test. The 10 m patch with hand-made UVs shows cracks, wheel paths and gutters; the city's own asphalt meshes still don't (open).
street: Pass 30 street scenes. Noon, golden hour, neon night, rain night, nitro, drift, traffic, close-up.

open: Wheel paths, oil, gutters and patches render on a test patch but not on the city's asphalt meshes, which are what you see; their UV data is the remaining suspect.
The glowing disc sits behind this car's rims and doesn't read; the HUD brake temperatures do.
